dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: bhāve tyakte niruddhā cin naiva bhāvāntaraṃ vrajet | tadā tanmadhyabhāvena vikasatyati bhāvanā ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
sanskrit_variants: verse 62: Singh records that the Kashmir Series edition reads bhāve nyakte; he follows bhāve tyakte (as GRETIL, Wallis and Pradīpaka do) on the authority of Jayaratha.
dharana.rendering: When one object of mind has been let go and awareness, restrained, does not move on to another, then through that in-between state contemplation blossoms intensely.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: verse 61 drops two positive perceptions; here the gap is between one object released and another that is not allowed to arise. Abhinavagupta refers to both (Tantrāloka 1.84, with Jayaratha's commentary). Singh notes that the Kashmir Series text reads bhāve nyakte ('fixed on an object never seen before') and argues that bhāve tyakte ('when an object is let go'), followed here, is the better reading.
dharana.technique_name: Not Moving On to the Next Thing
dharana.instruction: When a thought ends, don't reach for the next one; stay in the space it leaves.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 62 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the next object, not taken up
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is one point that has just been let go and an empty space where the next one would have come.
geometry.svg_hint: a fading dot on the left, an open highlighted space on the right where nothing has appeared
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Don't reach for the next
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the chain of one thought after another pauses after one link, and the pause opens. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: When something ends, do not reach for the next thing
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The moment after one thought or perception ends, before the next is taken up
attention.secondary: The opening of that in-between state

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: When one object of mind has been let go and awareness, restrained, does not move on to another, then through that in-between state contemplation blossoms intensely.
adiyogi.method_summary: Let one thought or perception end. Before reaching for the next, pause and stay in the space that is left. Do not suppress what comes; simply do not move on to it yet.

honesty.disclosure: Door 039 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 39 (verse 62) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 039 is dharana 39, verse 62. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. This is not forced blankness; if strain appears, let thoughts come and go freely. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
